title: Why Teenagers Can’t Fall Asleep Early
subtitle: 青少年為什麼早睡不著：生理時鐘的延後
source: 原創教學文章；內容依美國兒科學會（AAP）2014 年政策聲明〈School Start Times for Adolescents〉，2026-10-21 核對。本文不是醫療建議。

sources.title: American Academy of Pediatrics (2014). School Start Times for Adolescents. Pediatrics, 134(3), 642–649.

beginner.title: Not Lazy, Just Late
paras: Many teenagers hear the same words at home: “Go to bed earlier!” They try. They turn off the light at ten o’clock. But they lie in bed, wide awake, until eleven or later. In the morning, the alarm rings and they can hardly open their eyes. Are they lazy? Scientists say the answer is usually no.
很多青少年在家裡都聽過同一句話：「早點去睡！」他們也試了：十點就關燈，卻躺在床上清醒得很，直到十一點甚至更晚。到了早上，鬧鐘響了，他們幾乎睜不開眼。他們是懶嗎？科學家說，答案通常是否定的。

Everyone has a body clock. It tells us when to feel sleepy and when to feel awake. Around the start of puberty, this clock changes. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics, a large group of children’s doctors in the United States, many teenagers’ sleep times shift later by up to two hours.
每個人都有一個生理時鐘，告訴我們什麼時候會想睡、什麼時候會清醒。大約在青春期開始的時候，這個時鐘會改變。根據美國兒科學會——一個由美國兒科醫師組成的大型組織——許多青少年的睡眠時間會往後延，最多延後兩個小時。

One reason is a hormone called melatonin, which helps us feel sleepy. In teenagers, the body releases melatonin later at night. Because of this, the average teenager finds it hard to fall asleep before 11 p.m. and is best suited to wake up at 8 a.m. or later.
原因之一是一種叫褪黑激素的荷爾蒙，它會讓人想睡。青少年的身體在夜裡較晚才分泌褪黑激素。因此，一般青少年很難在晚上十一點前睡著，最適合的起床時間是早上八點或更晚。

At the same time, teenagers still need a lot of sleep — about 8.5 to 9.5 hours a night. If school starts very early, many students simply cannot get enough. Too little sleep can affect health, mood, safety and schoolwork.
同時，青少年仍然需要很多睡眠——每晚大約 8.5 到 9.5 小時。如果學校很早就上課，許多學生根本睡不夠。睡太少會影響健康、心情、安全和課業。

That is why, in 2014, the American Academy of Pediatrics recommended that middle and high schools start at 8:30 a.m. or later. Not every school can change its schedule. But understanding your body clock is a good first step. Being tired in the morning may not be a character problem. It may be biology.
這就是為什麼美國兒科學會在 2014 年建議，國中和高中應該在早上八點半或更晚才開始上課。不是每所學校都能改變作息，但了解自己的生理時鐘是很好的第一步。早上很累，不一定是個性的問題，可能是生理的問題。

intermediate.title: Why Teenagers Can’t Fall Asleep Early
paras: Teenagers have a reputation for staying up late and struggling to get out of bed. Parents often see this as a matter of discipline: if students simply went to bed earlier, the problem would disappear. Yet doctors who study adolescent sleep argue that the issue is not mainly about willpower. It is, to a large degree, about biology — and about the clock on the school wall.
青少年常被認為愛熬夜、早上爬不起來。家長往往把這當成自律問題：只要學生早點上床，問題就會消失。然而，研究青少年睡眠的醫師認為，這件事主要不是意志力的問題。在很大程度上，它和生理有關——也和教室牆上的那個時鐘有關。

In 2014, the American Academy of Pediatrics published a policy statement on school start times. It explained that, at about the time puberty begins, most adolescents experience a “phase delay”: their sleep and wake times shift later, by up to two hours compared with middle childhood. In other words, a body that once felt sleepy at nine o’clock may now feel alert until eleven. This change happens to most adolescents, not just to a few night owls.
2014 年，美國兒科學會發表了一份關於學校上課時間的政策聲明。聲明解釋，大約在青春期開始時，多數青少年會經歷「相位延遲」：他們的入睡和起床時間往後延，比童年中期最多晚兩個小時。換句話說，一個以前九點就想睡的身體，現在可能到十一點都還很清醒。這種改變發生在大多數青少年身上，而不只是少數夜貓子。

Two biological changes help explain this shift. First, the body releases melatonin, a hormone linked to sleepiness, later in the evening. Second, the pressure to fall asleep builds up more slowly during the day than it does in younger children. Together, these changes make it easier for teenagers to stay awake later. According to the statement, the average teenager has difficulty falling asleep before 11 p.m.
有兩個生理變化可以解釋這種延後。第一，身體在晚上較晚才分泌褪黑激素——一種與睏意有關的荷爾蒙。第二，白天累積的「睡意壓力」比年紀較小的孩子累積得慢。這兩項變化加在一起，讓青少年更容易晚睡。根據這份聲明，一般青少年很難在晚上十一點前入睡。

The problem is that teenagers’ need for sleep does not decrease. Most still need 8.5 to 9.5 hours a night. When school begins early, the gap between when students can fall asleep and when they must wake up leaves many of them chronically short of sleep. The AAP linked insufficient sleep to risks for physical and mental health, safety and academic performance. Napping, sleeping in on weekends and drinking coffee can hide the tiredness for a while, but the statement noted that they cannot replace regular, sufficient sleep.
問題在於，青少年對睡眠的需求並沒有減少，多數人每晚仍需要 8.5 到 9.5 小時。如果學校很早上課，學生「能睡著的時間」和「必須起床的時間」之間的落差，會讓很多人長期睡眠不足。美國兒科學會指出，睡眠不足與身心健康、安全和學業表現的風險都有關聯。午睡、週末補眠和喝咖啡，可以暫時掩蓋疲倦，但聲明指出，這些都無法取代規律而充足的睡眠。

For this reason, the AAP urged middle and high schools to aim for start times of 8:30 a.m. or later. The recommendation is not simple to put into practice: bus schedules, after-school activities and family routines all depend on the timetable. Still, the science offers a useful message for students themselves. Feeling exhausted in the morning is not necessarily a sign of laziness — and protecting sleep is not a luxury, but a basic part of learning well.
因此，美國兒科學會呼籲國中和高中把上課時間訂在早上八點半或更晚。這項建議要落實並不容易：校車班次、課後活動和家庭作息，全都跟著時間表走。儘管如此，這些科學研究對學生本身也有實用的啟示：早上筋疲力盡，不一定代表懶惰；而保護睡眠不是奢侈，是好好學習的基本條件。

advanced.title: The Clock Inside and the Clock on the Wall
paras: Few complaints are as universal among parents of teenagers as the one about sleep: adolescents stay up too late and cannot get up in the morning. The usual explanation is behavioral — late-night phone use, poor time management, a lack of discipline. These factors are real, but they leave out a crucial part of the picture. Much of the difficulty begins not in a teenager’s habits but in the timing of the body itself. Telling a teenager to “just go to bed earlier” assumes that sleep can be switched on at will, which is precisely what the biology makes difficult.
在青少年家長之間，很少有抱怨像睡眠問題這樣普遍：孩子太晚睡、早上起不來。常見的解釋是行為上的——深夜滑手機、時間管理差、缺乏自律。這些因素確實存在，卻漏掉了關鍵的一部分。許多困難的源頭，不在青少年的習慣，而在身體本身的時間設定。叫青少年「早點睡就好」，等於假設睡眠可以說開就開——而這正是生理條件讓人難以做到的。

In a 2014 policy statement, the American Academy of Pediatrics summarized decades of research on this question. Around the onset of puberty, it noted, most adolescents undergo a sleep–wake “phase delay”, a shift of up to two hours later relative to the sleep–wake cycles of middle childhood. A child who was once ready for bed at nine may, within a few years, feel genuinely alert at eleven.
在 2014 年的一份政策聲明中，美國兒科學會整理了數十年來對這個問題的研究。聲明指出，大約在青春期開始時，多數青少年會經歷睡眠—清醒週期的「相位延遲」，比童年中期最多延後兩個小時。一個以前九點就準備上床的孩子，幾年之內，可能到十一點都還真的很清醒。

Two mechanisms appear to drive this change. The first is the delayed timing of nighttime melatonin secretion, which parallels a shift from a “morning” to an “evening” preference. The second is an altered sleep drive: in older adolescents, the pressure to fall asleep accumulates more slowly across the day. Neither mechanism reduces how much sleep teenagers need. The statement put the optimal amount at 8.5 to 9.5 hours a night, and concluded that the average teenager has difficulty falling asleep before 11 p.m. and is best suited to wake at 8 a.m. or later. Put simply, adolescents are asked to fall asleep earlier at the very moment their bodies are telling them to stay up later.

有兩個機制似乎推動了這種改變。第一是夜間褪黑激素分泌時間的延後，這與從「晨型」轉向「夜型」偏好的變化同步。第二是睡眠驅力的改變：年紀較大的青少年，一天中累積睡意壓力的速度比較慢。這兩個機制都沒有減少青少年需要的睡眠量。聲明指出最理想的睡眠時間是每晚 8.5 到 9.5 小時，並總結：一般青少年很難在十一點前入睡，最適合在早上八點或更晚起床。簡單說，青少年被要求更早入睡的時候，恰好是他們的身體叫他們晚點睡的時候。

Set against this biology, an early school start creates a structural problem rather than a personal one. If a student cannot fall asleep before eleven and must leave home at six-thirty, no amount of good intentions will produce nine hours of sleep. The AAP therefore identified early start times as a key modifiable contributor to insufficient sleep, a condition it associated with poorer physical and mental health, drowsy-driving crashes and weaker academic performance. Weekend lie-ins, afternoon naps and caffeine may disguise the deficit temporarily, but, as the statement emphasized, they do not restore optimal alertness and are no substitute for regular sufficient sleep.

放在這樣的生理條件下來看，太早上課造成的是結構性問題，而不是個人問題。如果一個學生十一點前睡不著，卻必須在六點半出門，再好的意圖也換不來九小時的睡眠。因此，美國兒科學會把過早的上課時間，列為睡眠不足中一個可以調整的關鍵因素；而睡眠不足與較差的身心健康、疲勞駕駛車禍，以及較弱的學業表現都有關。週末補眠、午睡和咖啡因或許能暫時掩蓋睡眠負債，但如聲明所強調，它們無法恢復最佳的清醒程度，也無法取代規律而充足的睡眠。

Its recommendation was clear: middle and high schools should aim to start at 8:30 a.m. or later. Implementing such a change is complicated, since transport, sports and parents’ work schedules are all built around the existing timetable, and the statement itself acknowledged that the issue is controversial. Yet the underlying argument deserves attention well beyond the United States. When a system repeatedly asks young people to act against their own biology, the resulting exhaustion is better understood as a design problem than as a moral failing.
它的建議很明確：國中和高中應以早上八點半或更晚開始上課為目標。要落實這樣的改變很複雜，因為交通、運動和家長的工作時間，都是依現行時間表安排的；聲明本身也承認這個議題具有爭議。然而，這背後的論點值得美國以外的地方關注。當一個制度一再要求年輕人違背自己的生理運作，隨之而來的疲憊，與其說是道德缺陷，不如理解為設計上的問題。

vocab.example: Melatonin is a hormone that helps us sleep.
Tiredness is sometimes a matter of biology.
It takes willpower to put your phone away.
Adolescents need more sleep than adults.
Coffee makes me feel more alert.
Scientists study the mechanisms of memory.

phrases.usage: lie wide awake（躺著完全睡不著）。
phrases.example: I lay wide awake all night.

phrases.usage: 可表示「同時發生」，也可帶出相對的另一面。
phrases.example: The job is tiring. At the same time, it is rewarding.
phrases.writing: S + V. At the same time, S + V.

phrases.example: It is time to put the plan into practice.
phrases.writing: It is not simple to put + N + into practice.

phrases.example: Success depends to a large degree on effort.
phrases.writing: It is, to a large degree, about + N.

patterns.frame: S + find(s) it + adj. + to V
patterns.example: The average teenager finds it hard to fall asleep before 11 p.m.
patterns.tip: it 是虛受詞，真正的受詞是後面的 to V。

patterns.frame: A is not mainly about B; it is about C
patterns.meaning: A 主要不是 B 的問題，而是 C
patterns.example: The issue is not mainly about willpower. It is about biology.
patterns.tip: 用來重新定義一個問題。

patterns.frame: no amount of + N + will + V
patterns.example: No amount of good intentions will produce nine hours of sleep.
patterns.tip: 強調「不可能」的論說句型。

patterns.frame: A is better understood as B than as C
patterns.meaning: A 與其理解為 C，不如理解為 B
patterns.example: The exhaustion is better understood as a design problem than as a moral failing.
patterns.tip: 高階論說文常用的重新詮釋句型。

quote.text: Sleep, that knits up the ravell’d sleave of care, / The death of each day’s life, sore labour’s bath, / Balm of hurt minds, great nature’s second course, / Chief nourisher in life’s feast.
quote.author: William Shakespeare
quote.work: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 2（睡眠能把亂成一團的憂愁重新編好）

beginner.why: 第二段：最多延後兩小時。

Teenagers have more energy at night because of food

intermediate.q: Why is the AAP’s recommendation “not simple to put into practice”?
options: Bus schedules, activities and family routines depend on the timetable
It is too expensive to buy clocks
